title: Thiébou Dieun
author: Amina Savoura
desc: A kilo of thiof, a kilo of broken rice, and both fermented seasonings — a small piece of yet and a small piece of guedj — in a two-hour cook.
longDesc: The most completely specified of the documented thiébou dieun recipes where the fermented seasonings are concerned: it names both a small piece of yet and a small piece of guedj by quantity, which most printings leave out. A kilo of thiof goes with a kilo of rice broken once or twice, a quarter of a white cabbage, two carrots, a yam or sweet potato, a turnip, an African eggplant, two or three okra, and a hundred and forty grams of concentrated tomato. The rof stuffing is curly parsley, a chilli, two cloves of garlic, a bouillon cube and black pepper. Total cooking time as printed is two hours.
ingredients: 1 kg rice broken once or twice — brisures de riz
2 to 3 bouillon cubes, plus 1 adja cube (optional)
140 g concentrated tomato — one small tin
Salt, and pepper — very little pepper
// For the rof, the fish stuffing
steps: Pound the rof: curly parsley, chilli, garlic, bouillon cube and black pepper.
Slit the fish and stuff it with the rof.
Heat the oil and brown the fish in it — y faire dorer les poissons.
Add the onion and the concentrated tomato and let it simmer about 10 minutes, stirring.
Add the water, the yet and the guedj, the chilli and the bouillon.
Add the vegetables and let it cook 45 minutes.
Take the fish out after 20 minutes if you find it overcooked.
Remove the vegetables as soon as they are done.
Add the washed rice to the broth and finish the cooking.
chefTips: This is the printing to follow if you want the fermented seasonings specified — a small piece of yet AND a small piece of guedj, both named, which most versions omit or leave to taste.
Pull the fish at twenty minutes if it looks done. Her instruction is explicit and it is the right call — the vegetables need longer than the fish.
Remove each vegetable as it finishes rather than all together. They cook at very different rates.
Two hundred and fifty millilitres of oil is a lot and it is correct for the dish — the oil separating out is what the rice later absorbs.
Very little pepper, by her own note, despite the chilli. The heat comes from the Antillean chilli, not from black pepper.
A kilo of rice to a kilo of fish is a one-to-one ratio, which is the generous end. Scale the rice down before the fish if you want it lighter.
Rice broken once or twice, not three times — the degree of brokenness changes how much broth it drinks.
commonMistakes: Leaving the fish in for the full forty-five minutes.
Lifting all the vegetables out at once.
Cutting the oil, which starves the rice of the fat it needs.
sources: Adapted from 'thiébou dieun (riz au poisson)', afrik.com. BYLINE EXACTLY AS PRINTED: 'Amina Savoura'. Date as printed: 'Publié le 29 novembre 2017 à 22h26'. Yield as printed: 'pour 04 à 06 personnes'. Cooking time as printed: 'temps de cuisson: 2 heures'. TWO-PASS — pass one paraphrased, pass two returned the ingredient list verbatim, and the quantities AGREE across both.

Ingredient list as printed in French: '1kg de thiof (mérou)'; '1kg de riz cassé une ou deux fois (brisures de riz)'; '1/4 de choux blanc'; '2 carottes'; '1 igname ou 1 patate douce'; '1 navet'; 'une aubergine africaine (diakhato)'; '2/3 gombos (parce que j'aime bien!)'; '1 tomate fraîche'; '1 gros oignon'; 'un petit morceau de yet'; 'un petit morceau de guedj'; '1 piment antillais'; '2 à 3 bouillons maggi (+1 adja facultatif)'; '140g de tomates concentrée (une petite boîte)'; '250 ml d'huile'; 'sel, poivre (très peu de poivre)'. For the rof: 'un bouquet de persil frisé'; '1 piment'; '2 gousses d'ail'; '1 cube de bouillon maggi'; 'poivre noir'.

TWO PRINTED ODDITIES, reproduced and not corrected: '2/3 gombos' is a RANGE, two or three okra, not a fraction, and the parenthesis '(parce que j'aime bien!)' — because I like it — is the author's own aside; and '140g de tomates concentrée' carries a number disagreement in the French as printed.

Times and cues as printed in French: 'y faire dorer les poissons'; 'Laisser mijoter environ 10 minutes en remuant'; 'Laisser cuire 45 minutes.'; 'Enlever le poisson au bout de 20 minutes si vous les trouver trop cuits.' — printed 'vous les trouver', as printed; 'Retirer les légumes dés qu'ils sont cuits' — printed 'dés' for 'dès', as printed.

WHY THIS ENTRY IS PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE SEN001: it is the fullest documented treatment of the FERMENTED seasonings in a ceebu jen, naming both yet and guedj with quantities. The Thiam version gives them as 'palm-sized pieces' and '2 pieces'; this one gives 'un petit morceau' of each. Neither is corrected toward the other.

ON THE FERMENTED SEASONINGS: guedj and yet are used here as BOUGHT ingredients. Their own from-scratch processes are documented at SEN088 and SEN089 as traditional processes, with the finished-product description, the published rejection thresholds and the safety warnings; neither has an in-process doneness test, and that gap is stated plainly at those entries. Buying them is the stated default.
THE SERVINGS FIGURE above takes the midpoint of the printed 'pour 04 à 06 personnes'.

A NOTE ON THE QUOTE CAP, which applies to every Senegalese entry in this collection: the retrieval layer refuses verbatim transcription beyond roughly 125 characters per passage. The French strings above are short enough to be exact; nothing longer should be read as a single uninterrupted quotation.
reheating: Steam the rice; warm the fish and vegetables in broth.
healthBenefits: Grouper supplies protein, selenium and vitamin B12.
Seven vegetables plus okra in one pot.
Fermented fish seasonings contribute glutamates that cut the need for added salt.
culturalNote: Published on a pan-African news and culture site by a named Senegalese contributor, this is the version of ceebu jen that a Dakar household would recognise — including the bouillon cubes that purists leave out of printed recipes and everybody uses at home.
